cards.text: Friend, Ahab, king of Israel, is dead, and Moab rebels against Israel. His son Ahaziah is king now, and he worships Baal just like his dad did (1 Kings 22:51-53). Then one day in Samaria, Ahaziah falls through the lattice of his upper room and hurts himself.

cards.question: Ahaziah is hurt and wants to know if he'll recover. Who does he send messengers to ask?

answers.text: Elijah the prophet of the LORD

cards.text: So off the messengers go. But the angel of the LORD sends Elijah the Tishbite, a prophet of the LORD (1 Kings 18:22), to go up and meet them on their way.

cards.question: The angel of the LORD gives Elijah a question to ask the king's messengers. What is it?

answers.text: Is there no God in Israel
Who sent you down this road

cards.question: Ahaziah wanted to know if he'd recover. What does the LORD say will happen to him?

answers.text: He will heal in seven days

cards.text: So Elijah goes, and the messengers head right back to the king, who asks, “Why have you returned?” He sent them out, and here they are already, like hitting send and getting “Message not delivered.”

cards.question: Back with the king, the messengers keep the man's message to themselves.

cards.text: So Ahaziah just heard the LORD say he will surely die. And his next question is… describe the guy. What sort of man came up to meet you?

cards.question: How do the messengers describe the man who met them?

answers.text: A hairy man with a leather belt
A young man in royal robes
An old man leaning on a staff

cards.question: After hearing the description, Ahaziah has no idea who the man could be.

cards.text: Ahaziah doesn't need a second clue: “It was Elijah the Tishbite.” A hairy man with a leather belt isn't a description, friend, it's a BUSINESS CARD.
Then King Ahaziah sends a captain with his company of fifty men to Elijah, who's sitting on top of a hill. Fifty men. For one hairy guy who is SITTING DOWN.

cards.question: The first captain goes up to Elijah on the hill. What does he tell him?
Elijah answers the first captain with an if: if he is a man of God, then what should happen?

answers.text: Fire will come down from heaven
The hill will shake under them
The men will be struck blind

cards.question: Fire comes down from heaven and consumes the first captain and his fifty men.

cards.text: So the king sends another captain with his fifty men, and this one says, “Come down at once!” Fifty men just got consumed, friend, and this guy adds AT ONCE, like a man whose car is making a weird noise so he turns the radio UP.

cards.question: The second captain tells Elijah to come down at once. What does Elijah say back?

answers.text: The same words he said before

cards.question: This time the fire stays in heaven, and the second captain walks away.

cards.text: So the king sends a third captain with his fifty men, and I bet that man walked up the hill SLOW. But when he gets there, he does something the first two didn't.

cards.question: What does the third captain do when he reaches Elijah?

answers.text: He falls on his knees and begs
He orders Elijah down at once
He waits at the foot of the hill

cards.question: On his knees, the third captain begs Elijah that his life and the lives of his fifty men would be ___ in Elijah's sight.

cards.text: Then the angel of the LORD speaks to Elijah again, right there on that hill.

cards.question: What does the angel of the LORD tell Elijah to do about the third captain?

answers.text: Go down with him without fear
Call fire down on him too
Stay up on the hill for now

cards.question: Elijah gets up and goes down with the third captain to the king.

cards.text: Now Elijah speaks the LORD's word to King Ahaziah himself, face to face: “Is there really no God in Israel for you to inquire of His word?” Then that ending again: “You will surely die.”

cards.question: Elijah has told Ahaziah the LORD's word in person. What happens to the king?

answers.text: He dies as the LORD said
He gets up from his bed

cards.question: Ahaziah had no son. Who becomes king of Israel in his place?

cards.text: And this Jehoram takes over in the second year of the reign of Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat over Judah, so now BOTH kingdoms have a Jehoram, and somebody is DEFINITELY getting the other guy's mail. The rest of Ahaziah's acts are written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 11 quotes "It was Elijah the Tishbite.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The card opens by retelling the message from 1:6 ('Ahaziah just heard the LORD say he will surely die') and then tells 1:7, but it cites only 2 Kings 1:7. The citation should be 2 Kings 1:6-7.

rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The setup on card 8 rules out both wrong answers. It says the third captain 'does something the first two didn't', and the first two ordered Elijah down, which removes 'He orders Elijah down at once'. It also says 'when he gets there', and the question says 'when he reaches Elijah', which removes 'He waits at the foot of the hill'. Only the right answer is left.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: In 2 Kings 1:10, Elijah says 'may fire come down from heaven', which is a call for fire. The right answer, 'Fire will come down from heaven', turns that call into a prediction.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: Two jokes build on how Elijah looks. Here he is 'one hairy guy who is SITTING DOWN', and stop 1 card 11 calls 'a hairy man with a leather belt' a BUSINESS CARD. The description comes straight from 2 Kings 1:8, and neither joke is a putdown, but calling a prophet 'one hairy guy' may not look at him with respect.
findings.question: The hard rules say no jokes about appearance, and Bible people must be treated with respect. Do those rules allow a joke that uses a person's physical description from the text when the joke isn't a putdown? If they do, is 'one hairy guy' respectful enough for Elijah?
